quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How do you brake hardest in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: The best braking happens when you apply both the front and rear brakes together. Make sure neither wheel locks up.

questions.question: What should you do if the throttle gets stuck?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle sticks, twist it back and forth several times. If it still does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle crash deaths involved riders who had been drinking?

options.text: 20 percent
40 percent
60 percent
80 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Studies show that about 40 percent of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking. Alcohol is a major cause of fatal motorcycle accidents.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, but not both.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Never brake and swerve at the same time. Do one action first, then the other. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: How many motorcycle-car crashes are caused by drivers not yielding the right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to riders.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?

options.text: Before the engine starts.
After the engine starts.
While sitting as far back as possible.
While holding onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should mount only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider's control. They should hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When is a larger space cushion between you and the car ahead not necessary?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
When traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in bad conditions. You need more space if the pavement is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What should you do if your front tire locks while braking?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever so the tire can grip again. Then apply the brake again.

questions.question: What should a proper lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Give you an escape route.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When you prepare to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they often seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling more slowly than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.
Closer than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may look like they are going faster than they really are because of their small size.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: Passing another vehicle.
You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is not as visible as the two larger lights on cars or trucks. Flash your brake light when you slow down quickly so other drivers notice it in time.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. It also tells other drivers your plans and gives you an escape route if needed. A lane position does not help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: A close group takes up minimal space.
A close group is usually easier to see than a group that is spread out.
A close group is less likely to get separated than a group that is spread out.
A close group can ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: A close group can ride in pairs.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close, tight group is better than spreading out because it takes less road space, is easier for others to see, and riders stay together at traffic lights. A staggered formation is safer than riding in pairs.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Group signals are important for communication. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: Good rain suits:

options.text: Should not be used.
Should not balloon when riding.
Are not needed since motorcycles shouldn't be operated in the rain.
Should tear easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not balloon when riding.
questions.explanation: Quality motorcycle rain suits will not tear or balloon out when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: If you must swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn your handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn. To turn left, press the left handlebar, then the right to straighten. To turn right, press the right handlebar, then the left.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Debris and oil drippings from cars collect in the center of a traffic lane. Where else can you find hazards like this?

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect there.
Motorcycle riders should always travel there for safety.
Most accidents happen there.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect there.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane collects debris and oil drippings from cars. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also found in the center of lanes.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
Separate occasionally.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders should stay close together while keeping enough space to maneuver safely. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from becoming separated. Pairing up does not give riders enough space to maneuver.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points it upward?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals. When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points it upward, it signals a right turn or lane change to the right.

questions.question: When riding in a group, which is the best practice?

options.text: Never use a staggered formation.
Place inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Not use your mirrors.
Not tailgate other riders within the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not tailgate other riders within the group.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check your mirrors often. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
They happen at night.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Continue using the rear brake.
Swerve the bike in the direction with the fewest hazards.
Try to accelerate while the brake is engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, on a good surface, you can keep the rear brake locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel begins to skid?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Immediately release and re-engage the front brake.
Release the front brake and increase pressure on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately release and re-engage the front brake.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then smoothly apply the front brake again.

questions.question: What should you do if you lock the rear tire on a good road surface?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good road surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar during acceleration?

options.text: It feels like it is lagging behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
It vibrates uncontrollably.
It makes acceleration seem faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is lagging behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered mass attached to your motorcycle. Because of its weight and inertia, it feels like it lags behind when you accelerate.

questions.question: How should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Do not use it.
Use the high beam setting.
Use the low beam setting.
Alternate between high beam and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the high beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam during the day when you are not behind or approaching other vehicles. High beams make other drivers more likely to see you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show road rules like speed limits. These regulatory signs are white with black text or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay on the left side of the lane.
Always stay on the right side of the lane.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve may not match the shape of the road.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses underneath.
Block your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Push the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pushing the grip in your desired direction makes the motorcycle lean correctly for the turn.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Shifting into neutral gear.
You will slow down suddenly.
A stop sign is ahead.
Your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly, especially if someone is following too closely. The driver behind you may not see road hazards ahead that are making you slow down.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Go faster.
Follow other vehicles more closely.
Use headlights from vehicles ahead to see the road.
Wear dark glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use headlights from vehicles ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: To stay safe when riding at night, slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the right side of the lane.
Move onto the shoulder.
Turn on your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When someone is passing you from behind or from ahead, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you NOT use?

options.text: Plan travel distances based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan route length based on your least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce tiredness. Put new riders behind experienced leaders who can watch them. Use a staggered riding formation for safety.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply the brake when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes together. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply at the same time. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual to learn about your specific braking system.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and provides protection. Many jackets are made to keep riders cool, even when it is warm outside.

questions.question: When following a car, where in the lane should you ride?

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The left or right portions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors, so this position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need?

options.text: Much less distance than cars.
Less distance than cars.
The same distance as cars.
More distance than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance as cars.
questions.explanation: In traffic, motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always the right portion of the lane.
Always the center portion of the lane.
Always the left portion of the lane.
It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on how conditions change while you ride.

questions.question: What should a passenger never do?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers should wear fitted clothing and lean with the operator when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The center portion.
The left portion.
The right portion.
Any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from moving back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a dry surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a dry surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels in a straight line.

questions.question: What is your best protection while riding?

options.text: Keeping space between you and other vehicles.
Wearing a leather jacket.
Wearing sturdy boots.
Knowing motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your best protection is to stay far away from other vehicles. This gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move forward.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. The vehicle may back up unexpectedly, or you may need space to move if another vehicle comes from behind.
